paper_title: Iron-Catalyzed Aerobic Oxidation of Allylic Alcohols: The Issue of C=C Bond Isomerization

questions.question: In this paper, what does the label 'E-1a' refer to?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The E-isomer of substrate 1a — the (E)-configured allylic alcohol used as the model substrate in the optimization and scale‑up experiments (E-1a, stated as E/Z = 99/1 in the paper; structure shown in Table 1 and Scheme 2).

questions.question: What is the chemical composition (formula/IUPAC) of the catalyst referred to as 'Fe(NO3)3·9H2O' in the experiments?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Iron(III) nitrate nonahydrate, formula Fe(NO3)3·9H2O (used as the iron catalyst in the reported oxidations).

questions.question: According to the optimized room‑temperature procedure used to oxidize E-1a to E-2a (as reported in the abstract/Table 1), what solvent, catalyst/TEMPO/NaCl loadings, atmosphere, and temperature were used?
questions.ground_truth_answer: DCE (0.1 M); 10 mol % Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 10 mol % TEMPO, 10 mol % NaCl; O2 (atmospheric oxygen); room temperature (rt).

questions.question: In Table 1, which entry gave the higher isolated yield for conversion of E-1a to 2a — entry 1 (conc. = 5.0, 12 h) or entry 9 (conc. = 0.1, 3 h) — and what were the reported yields and E/Z ratios for those entries?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Entry 1 gave a slightly higher yield: entry 1 — 98% yield (reported) with E/Z = 80/20; entry 9 — 95% yield with E/Z = 97/3.

questions.question: What isolated yield and E/Z ratio were obtained in the reported 0.1 mmol scale oxidation of E-1a to give E-2a under the optimized conditions (scale‑up/test experiment shown in Scheme 2)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 90% isolated yield after 6 h; product E-2a obtained with E/Z = 97/3 (starting E-1a was E/Z = 99/1).
